tagline: Premium digital journalism and subscription-based media company
hero_kpi_rationale: The number of digital subscribers is the primary driver of revenue growth and directly reflects the success of the company's digital transformation strategy.

kpis.name: Total Subscribers
kpis.explanation: Total number of subscribers to print and digital products.
kpis.description: Total subscriber count, including digital and print subscribers, is a key indicator of the reach and engagement of the user base.
kpis.signal: Continued growth in digital and print subscribers.

kpis.name: Digital-only Subscribers
kpis.explanation: Number of subscribers to exclusively digital products.
kpis.description: This KPI measures the traction of the digital transition strategy, a central element of the company's business model.

kpis.name: Digital-only ARPU
kpis.explanation: Average revenue generated per digital subscriber on a monthly basis.
kpis.description: Indicates the ability to monetize the digital subscriber base, potentially reflecting price increases or changes in subscription mix.
kpis.signal: Increase in revenue per digital subscriber.

kpis.name: Cash and Marketable Securities
kpis.explanation: Total amount of cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities held by the company.
kpis.description: Indicates the company's liquidity and financial flexibility for operations, investments, and shareholder returns.

kpis.name: Debt-free Status
kpis.explanation: The company has no debt on its balance sheet.
kpis.description: The absence of debt reduces financial risk and increases operational and strategic flexibility.

kpis.name: Share Repurchases
kpis.explanation: Amount of shares repurchased by the company during the fiscal year.
kpis.description: Indicates the capital return policy to shareholders, complementing dividends and optimizing capital structure.
kpis.signal: Capital return to shareholders via repurchases.

kpis.name: Dividend per Share
kpis.explanation: Amount of dividend paid per share (quarterly dividend approved in February 2026).
kpis.description: Reflects the value distribution policy to shareholders and confidence in the company's future performance.

kpis.name: Total Revenue
kpis.description: Revenue extracted from SEC EDGAR companyfacts XBRL for the last 8 reported fiscal years (10-K).
kpis.signal: Revenue of $1.784B for the last fiscal year (FY2020).

kpis.name: Dividend per Share
kpis.description: Annual dividend per share paid, aggregated from yfinance.dividends for the last 7 fiscal years reported by the company.
kpis.signal: Dividend per share of $0.41 for the last year.

kpis.name: Capital Returned (Dividends)
kpis.description: Capital returned to shareholders via annual dividends, extracted from yfinance.cashflow for the last 4 reported fiscal years.
kpis.signal: Capital returned to shareholders via dividends of $0.11B for the last year.

kpis.name: Payout Ratio
kpis.description: Payout Ratio = Dividends paid / Net income, calculated for the last 4 fiscal years from yfinance.cashflow and yfinance.income_stmt.
kpis.signal: Share of net income distributed as dividends: 32.1% for the last year.

kpis.name: Bundle and Multi-product Subscribers
kpis.explanation: Number of digital subscribers who subscribe to bundled or multi-product offerings.
kpis.description: Indicates the cross-selling strategy and ability to increase value per subscriber through combined and packaged offerings.

kpis.name: Earnings per Share
kpis.explanation: Net income divided by the average number of diluted shares for the fiscal year. Shows the company's ability to generate earnings per share: the basis for calculating the Payout Ratio (DPS / EPS).
kpis.description: 5-year history (2021-2025). Source: yfinance income statement (Diluted EPS).

risks.title: Generative AI Litigation
risks.summary: Lawsuits over unauthorized use of content in AI training threaten profitability and reputation.
risks.score_rationale: The risk is explicitly mentioned with a 23.3% cost increase in one year, indicating escalation. The language emphasizes recurring and growing costs, and the topic is new in operating expenses. The 'Litigation' category is highly critical in media.

risks.title: Pension Cost Volatility
risks.summary: Pension obligations, while well-managed, remain sensitive to interest rates and markets, impacting financial stability.
risks.score_rationale: The risk is recurring (cited p.33-34), with explicit mention of volatility due to discount rates and returns. The adjustment amounts are increasing ($2,967M in 2025 vs -$2,980M in 2024). The size of obligations weighs on results.

risks.title: Digital Growth Dependency
risks.summary: Digital transition is succeeding, but declining news-only subscribers raise concerns about long-term loyalty.
risks.score_rationale: Revenue growth relies on digital subscriptions (+14.3%), but 'news-only' subscribers dropped 27%. The risk is implicit but central: loss of relevance for the flagship product. The change in segment reporting reinforces this concern.

risks.title: Future Multiemployer Pension Contributions
risks.summary: Past commitments to multiemployer plans could result in unexpected payments.
risks.score_rationale: Mention of 'additional' future obligations for multiemployer pensions (p.34), without a specific amount. The risk is latent but real, especially after a negative adjustment in 2025. 'Capital' category weighted medium.

risks.title: Decline in Print and Digital News-only Subscribers
risks.summary: The traditional subscriber base is shrinking, threatening the historical model despite bundle offering growth.
risks.score_rationale: Loss of 620,000 'news-only' subscribers (-27%) and -40,000 print subscribers in one year (p.36). The language is factual but trends are structural. Direct impact on core business.

risks.title: Shareholder Over-distribution Risk
risks.summary: The aggressive distribution policy could limit investment capacity during periods of pressure.
risks.score_rationale: Commitment to distribute 50% of FCF, while AI and pension costs are rising. The balance sheet is healthy ($1.2B in cash), but the risk is compromising financial flexibility if revenue slows.

ai_positioning.summary: NYT does not mention artificial intelligence in its report. There is no significant mention of AI or machine learning in the provided text.
